validated_public_error_diagnostic.diagnosis: Recorded compiler failure; does not establish a hardware or support limitation.

failure_diagnosis.confirmed_final_cause: The benchmark backend compile-attempt guard fired at 33 attempts with maximum 32. The final error chain was BackendCompilerFailed -> ValueError(public_cpu_compile_benchmark_invalid), not CppCompileError.
failure_diagnosis.recorded_execution_counter_reliability: The execute callback uses functools.wraps(compiled), which copies any _torchdynamo_orig_callable attribute from the returned backend callable. PyTorch 2.8 DisableContext calls innermost_fn, which follows this attribute. This can unwrap past the execution counter. Therefore the recorded zero counter is not proof that no compiled graph actually executed.
next_experiment_candidates: Return a plain execution-counter closure without functools.wraps(compiled) or copying compiler private attributes; add an unwrap-regression test.

Bound the next experiment explicitly at 64 or 96 backend compile attempts, retaining the 360-second per-call deadline and compile_threads=1. Do not change model, precision, sampler or mask calculations.
failure_diagnosis.interpretation: Mask isolation advanced past the earlier four-attempt C++ compile failure, but this trial did not complete a compiled WAV and does not establish a speed improvement.

PyTorch 2.8 innermost_fn follows that attribute and can unwrap past the callback. The saved zero is an observed counter value, not proof that no compiled graph ran.
